title: Canon in D
about: Johann Pachelbel wrote this canon around 1700, for three violins over a bass line. The bass plays the same eight notes again and again, while each violin enters with the same tune. The piece lay forgotten until Max Seiffert first printed it in 1919.
funFact: The canon was almost unknown until the late 1960s, and today it is one of the most played pieces at weddings.

practice.text: Play the right hand alone, slowly, and let the song wait for each note.
Now the left hand alone. The same eight notes come back three times.
Put both hands together on the first four bars.
Play the whole song with both hands at full speed.

tips.text: The tune walks down one key at a time, from finger 5 to the thumb.
Each bass note lasts two beats. Let it ring under the tune.
The tune now moves in quarter notes, twice as fast as before. Count four in each bar.

tricky.text: Move the hand one key lower: finger 2 goes from G to F, and the thumb takes E.
Finger 3 plays F and finger 2 plays D, so the thumb is ready for C.
Finger 5 comes back to C at the top, and the tune walks down again.

practice.text: Play the right hand alone through the falling line, slowly.
Play the left hand alone: a low note with finger 5, then a higher one with the thumb.
Play the thirds of bars 13 and 14 alone, and press both notes of each pair as one.
Play the whole song with both hands, a little slower than written.
Now play it at full speed.

tips.text: The bass walks the same eight notes all through the piece. Keep it soft and even.
The tune now moves on every beat, while the bass keeps its steady pace.
The lower notes of these thirds are the second violin. It plays the same tune, a third below.

tricky.text: End the bar with the thumb on G. Finger 5 then reaches up to F sharp.
Finger 4 moves from C sharp down to B, and the hand slides one key lower.
Finger 3 takes G and finger 2 takes E, so the thumb is ready for D.

practice.text: Play the Alberti bass alone until it rolls by itself: low, high, middle, high.
Play the right hand's sixths alone. Keep the hand in one shape and move it as a block.
Play the run of bars 13 to 16 alone, slowly, with the fingers written.
Play the whole song with both hands at three quarters speed.
Now play it at full speed, with the pedal.

tips.text: Keep the Alberti bass soft, so the long notes of the tune sing above it.
Thumb and finger 4 play every sixth. The tune is the top note.
Lift the pedal for the run, so each quick note stays clear.

tricky.text: From the last E, open the hand to D, F sharp and the high D in one move.
Fingers 3 and 2 cross over the thumb as the run falls. Keep the wrist still.
Slide the sixth down one key at a time. Thumb and finger 4 keep their shape.

practice.text: Play the octave bass alone: hold each octave, then lift the hand for the next one.
Play the right hand's chords alone, and let the top finger sing the tune.
Play the sixteenths of the left hand alone until they flow.
Join the hands on the whole song at three quarters speed.
Now play it at full speed, and make the last chord ring.

tips.text: Keep thumb and little finger an octave apart, and move the hand as one shape.
Play the top note of each chord a little louder than the others.
The left hand's sixteenths are a soft carpet. Keep them light and even.

tricky.text: The left hand starts its sixteenths here. Begin slowly, and let the tune walk on top.
The left hand jumps up to the D octave, while the right thumb steps from E to F sharp.
The thumb stays on F sharp for both chords. Move only fingers 3 and 5.
